title: CASE-09 — Delay crossing 31 March: the 43B(h) deferral has a real checkpoint
note: INPUT ONLY, synthetic (golden rule 11): no real parties, Udyam or GSTIN numbers. No outputs are stored here; every number comes from the engine. This case exists so the buyer's 43B(h) timing cost is not hypothetical: the delay runs across a 31 March financial-year close, so the deferral line actually computes and the CFO assumptions panel visibly moves its figures.
why_calculation_date: Deliberate: delivery 2026-11-15 plus 30 agreed days puts the due date on 2026-12-15, and the 2027-05-31 calculation date carries the delay across the 31 March 2027 year end. That 31 March is the only checkpoint the contract emits (fy_end, unpaid_principal, tax_timing_effect), and it is what makes the deferral line apply at all - no other shipped preset crosses a year end, so their deferral line is legitimately empty. The whole delay sits after the 2026-10-07 Bank Rate epoch, so it prices at a single configured rate (17.25%) and the case is about 43B(h), not about rate changes; that comparison is CASE-01's job.
